title: Anon by Anne Washburn at MCC #anon #mcctheater #broadwayreview #offbr...
transcript: When a play's subtitle is “a tempest at our kitchen table,” I'm hoping for something explosive and turbulent — Anon doesn't really deliver this. There's actually barely any conflict in the first act, though the exposition is well-crafted and compelling. We go back and forth between two households across the street from one another — a gay couple new to the neighborhood, and a housewife-turned-internet-warrior who is neck-deep in conspiracy theories. It's a little close for comfort thematically, and more explicitly political than it needs to be. The dynamics between characters are far more interesting than what I believe the piece is trying to say about how strong our confirmation biases are and how obsessive we can be in our political bubbles. Given how funny the dialogue is, how well the piece moves, and how good the acting is, it's a shame that it falls apart in Act 2. There's a remarkably interesting setup toward the end of Act 1 that's just never followed up on, and out of the multitude of possible ways the play could escalate, what actually happens leaves much to be desired from a plot standpoint. If we're calling it a character study, though, Crystal Finn's incredible performance practically redeems it. With that, another program for my collection.
